Welcome #2 SMS subject and preview test

heartbeat.title: Intrigue and self-relevance beat full explanation
heartbeat.body_html: Four of this month's winners point the same way. In Site Abandon, an open-loop message that hinted at a difference without spelling it out drove more clicks than a complete problem and solution. In Abandoned Checkout, stripping the copy down to raw product proof beat the conversational version for buyers who already have intent. And across the Welcome Flow, leading with Numin's own reframe ("you're not unfocused, you're full") and second-person "your brain" language lifted opens and clicks by making the message feel personal. The transferable lesson: readers respond to language that feels relevant and leaves a loop to close, more than to copy that over-explains. We are already carrying this into upcoming tests.

narrative.html: Flows earned 1,448 USD, up 394.5% on the prior month. Revenue per email delivered climbed from 0.081 to 0.574 USD, a sharp jump in how hard each send is working.

Flows returned to 9.8% of total store revenue, up from 2.0% last month and a clear step back toward the levels seen earlier in the series. This came from flow performance, not a broader lift in store demand.

Flows earn 8.1x more per email than campaigns (0.574 vs 0.071 USD RPR), and now account for 41% of email revenue. Deliverability stayed clean, with unsubscribes at 0.268% and spam complaints at 0.025%.

Campaigns sent 11 sends this month at 0.071 USD per email. Campaigns are your team's to run and you know the audience best. If it would ever help to have a second set of eyes on them, we are happy to take a look, no strings attached.

monthly.title_sub: Flows had a strong month, nearly quintupling revenue and reclaiming a much larger share of the store's total.

tests.what: Contextual "today" urgency versus general welcome messaging
Shorter, direct welcome SMS with faster decision framing
Immediate problem-solution framing versus reflective checkout copy
Subject mirroring hero message with browse-intent curiosity
"Better decisions start here" versus playful stay-sharp angle

heartbeat.title: Anchor the message to the moment
heartbeat.body_html: The clearest pattern across July's wins was immediacy. In the Welcome Flow, tying copy to "today" and condensing SMS into a faster decision beat the general messaging, and in Browse Abandon, subject lines that mirrored the email's core promise and leaned into "you paused for a reason" curiosity outperformed broader angles. The transferable lesson is that language anchored to a real, present moment converts better than generic framing. We are already rolling that principle into the next round of tests, which is the everyday work of keeping these flows sharp.

narrative.html: Flows earned $293 in July, down 57.1% from last month, and flow share of total store revenue eased to 2.0%. Revenue per email delivered came in at $0.081 against $0.129 prior, so the pullback is real rather than a volume artefact. This tracks a quieter store overall, and it is the number we are focused on lifting next month.

Four of five A/B tests won this month, an 80% win rate, with gains landing in the Welcome, Browse Abandon and Checkout journeys. Every win is now permanent in the flows, working on autopilot regardless of a slower sales month.

Flows earned $0.081 per email versus $0.093 on campaigns, about 0.9x. That is close, and with the winning copy and subject-line changes now live, we expect the per-email figure on flows to recover as the tested variants compound.

Campaigns sent 13 times and carried 92% of email revenue this month. Campaigns are your team's to run and they are doing the heavy lifting right now. If it is ever useful, we are happy to glance over the campaign side and share notes, no strings attached.

monthly.title_sub: Flows earned $293 in July, a softer month against a store that itself pulled back, with our testing program banking four more wins.
